subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this as the shared contract for runtime localization, locale ownership, command and skill metadata, and release coverage—and should script tags remain distinct from region tags?
rationale: The repository lifecycle and the proposal leave several durable product and compatibility contracts for owners to approve; source inspection cannot safely determine that intent.

options.title: Continue and revise the draft
options.body: Correct the locale identity model and obtain explicit decisions from each affected owner before acceptance.

options.title: Narrow the first RFC
options.body: Cover only locale resolution and runtime message descriptors, moving metadata and release coverage into later RFCs.

options.title: Decline the shared contract
options.body: Keep localization ownership surface-specific and address the linked gaps independently.

recommendation.title: Continue and revise the draft
recommendation.body: Correct the locale identity model and obtain explicit decisions from each affected owner before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest visible participant in prior project-level localization direction, while command-catalog ownership is shared with samzong and frankekn.
